findings.title: Praise as a tested and grateful verdict
findings.claim: The praise named by al-ḥamdu can be heard as both commendation and grateful recognition of what proves praiseworthy after outcomes are disclosed.
findings.mechanism: The focus morpheme 1:2:1:2 carries the ordinary praise relation through both supplied ḥamd facets; the later favor-and-adverse-outcome field and the supplied exact praise settings meet that carrier, changing praise from an unlocated formula into an evaluation of what the disclosed order yields.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can hear the opening praise as a response that remains praise while also carrying the sense of recognition after consequences become visible.
findings.containment: Ordinary praise remains the primary reading. The tested or grateful coloration is a contextual resonance of this ayah and its supplied connections, not a claim that every ḥamd use has this force or that this is a surah thesis.

epistemic.reason: The citable cross-run publication is explicitly anchored to both focus ḥamd branches; the connections supply exact Arabic settings and a live contrary ingratitude relation.

branch_activations.carrier: The focus form al-ḥamdu carries praise and commendation.

branch_activations.activation: The ordinary praise carrier meets later outcome and response contexts, so commendation is heard as recognition of what the disclosed order has shown.
branch_activations.resulting_reading: Praise remains praise while becoming a grateful evaluation of the one whose order is encountered.
branch_activations.boundary: This does not turn every praise use into thanksgiving or make the contextual evaluation a replacement for the plain nominal assertion.

branch_activations.resulting_reading: The opening praise can be heard as a verdict formed as the order and its consequences come into view.
branch_activations.boundary: The packet supports a contextual testing relation, not a claim that the focus grammar becomes a finite act or that one semantic facet excludes the other.

findings.title: Lordship cultivates legible worlds
findings.claim: The phrase Rabb al-ʿālamīn can carry a relation in which Lordship develops and completes worlds whose distinctions make orientation possible.
findings.mechanism: The focus forms Rabb and al-ʿālamīn carry stagewise nurture and distinguishing-sign facets; the supplied path and guidance relations, together with exact recognition-of-signs and guided-path connections, activate their contact and change worlds from a bare totality into an intelligible field under care.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can perceive care and worldhood together as an ordered field in which distinctions remain meaningful and movement can be guided.
findings.containment: The ordinary reading of the Lord of the worlds remains intact. The cultivated-legibility relation is a bounded global resonance; it does not replace worlds with signs or claim that all dictionary senses of either root are active.

epistemic.reason: The citable publication explicitly anchors the Rbb completion facet and the Elm sign facet, while the supplied connections provide independent guidance and recognition settings.

branch_activations.independent_trigger: The supplied path, guidance, sign-recognition, and differentiated-outcome contexts require an order that can be maintained through stages.
branch_activations.activation: Stagewise care meets the marked-world image, so the Lordship title can be read as sustaining the conditions in which the worlds become navigable.
branch_activations.resulting_reading: Lordship appears as ongoing cultivation toward an intelligible, usable order.
branch_activations.boundary: No claim is made that the title loses its ordinary ownership or governance relation.

findings.reader_payoff: The reader hears Lordship as a relation that reaches the conduct of those addressed, not only as a statement about divine scale.
findings.containment: Care and ordinary lordship remain present. The allegiance implication is a contextual global resonance, not a denial of the nurturing facet or a surah-wide selection.

epistemic.reason: The publication is citable and anchored to the qualified Rbb authority branch; the packet supplies independent worship and Lord-directed desire settings.

epistemic.reason: The walk supplies focus branch carriers and an explicit contextual favor relation, but the nominated favor branch is available only as a contextual source image.

findings.title: Praise grounded in received benefit

findings.mechanism: The focus al-ḥamdu carrier supplies commendation, while the supplied bestowed-favor context and exact received-gift, public-benefaction, and ingratitude connections provide an independent benefaction field that turns praise into evidence-bearing gratitude.

findings.containment: Gratitude is an activated coloring, not the whole lexical meaning of hamd. The adverse and non-transactional counter-relations remain available and are not ranked away.

epistemic.reason: The reader walk supplies the focus praise branch and a nominated favor image; the packet's connections provide independent benefaction and counter-evidence settings.

findings.containment: This is a qualified retrospective reader-walk synthesis, not a new lexical gloss and not a surah thesis. Praise and worlds remain separately recoverable; neither is ranked over the other.

epistemic.reason: The retrospective walk explicitly names the later favor and path feedback to the focus, but its reader identity is legacy-unbound and the context surface is not fully supplied.
